newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Honduran army chief survives gunfire attack.
newsitem.headline: Honduran army chief survives gunfire attack.

text.p: Honduran army chief Gen. Mario Hung escaped unhurt from an armed attack on his caravan, Honduran Radio America reported on Sunday.
Honduras' Criminal Investigations Directorate confirmed to reporters an attack took place on Saturday night but said that it could not provide details until the investigation was complete.

Unknown assailants sprayed Hung's vehicle with gunfire as he returned to Tegucigalpa with his family from his 50th birthday party at a military installation 15 miles (25 km) north of the capital, Radio America said.
An ambulance and two security vehicles in the general's caravan were also hit by gunfire, the report said.
When soliders investigated they found that the assailants had escaped, the radio report said.

Hung assumed the top military post in this Central American country in January 1996 and has since been considered a hardline defender of military power and privileges as President Carlos Roberto Reina has attempted to seize greater civilian control of the armed forces.
The traditionally powerful Honduran army has experienced periodic power struggles with three military chiefs being ousted from their posts in the past 15 years.
